subject: Request: short-term carve for ClearHealth AI onboarding sprint
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: short-term carve for ClearHealth AI onboarding sprint

Hi Ops/Product —

Quick context: ClearHealth AI (pilot customer; deal in negotiation — DEAL-4981) needs a hands-on onboarding sprint the week of Nov 22 for integration, low-latency validation, and a short stress test. They specifically asked for dedicated capacity during the onboarding window so their SREs can reproduce timing-sensitive flows.

What I’m requesting:
- Temporary carve of dedicated GPU slots from the enterprise pool for Nov 20 00:00 UTC through Nov 29 23:59 UTC (10 full days).
- Capacity target: equivalent of 4x A100-80GB (or 8x A30) throughout the window; burstable to +2 slots for evening tests.
- Autoscaling policy exception: keep reserved slots pinned to this carve (no preemption) for the window, with an ops rollback plan.

Why: customer insisted on predictable latency for their integration test and has signaled willingness to commit to a 6-month reserved contract if we can guarantee this onboarding experience. Sales (Neha) is coordinating incentives.

Attachments: onboarding_plan.xlsx (high-level schedule + tests).

Asks for Ops: can you confirm feasibility and list impacts (SLO, eviction risk, monitoring hooks) by EOD Wednesday?
Asks for Product: any product constraints to be aware of (model version pinning, telemetry access)?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term carve for ClearHealth AI onboarding sprint

Kimberly —

Thanks for the heads-up and the plan. Short answer: we can probably support a limited carve but need to scope operational impact. Quick notes from infra: 

- Current pool utilization (us-east) is at ~78% with a few enterprise pilots scheduled later this month. Carving 4x A100-equivalent continuously will increase utilization to ~92% during the window.
- We cannot guarantee zero preemption if capacity pressure spikes from critical internal runs. We can, however, provide a pinned reservation for the *daytime business hours* (08:00–20:00 UTC) and allow preemption outside that window — as an intermediate guarantee.
- Ops checklist / requirements: monitoring dashboards, a rollback playbook (eviction/requeue strategy), and a throttling policy for burst tests.

Proposal:
1) Immediate: create a short-lived carve for 2x A100-eq (minimum) for Nov 20–29 to unblock early onboarding; this is non-preemptible during 08:00–20:00 UTC.
2) Contingent: if other pilots are moved or load drops by Nov 18, we can scale to 4x A100-eq.
3) All carveouts to be tracked under INFRA-7382 (see Atlassian link).

Operational asks of Sales/Product team before we finalize:
- Confirm the strictness of the non-preemptible window (do we need 24/7 pinning or is daytime sufficient?).
- Approve the automated eviction fallback we’ll run if absolute capacity exhaustion occurs (safe-kill policy that prioritizes internal training runs over pilot).

I’ll kick off a quick capacity simulation and share numbers by EOD Tuesday. If you want immediate priority, we can move to a formal exception path but that will require a short-term credit charge to the customer or approval from Finance.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term carve for ClearHealth AI onboarding sprint

Thanks — good summary. A few product-side constraints and mitigations: 

- Model pinning: for deterministic latency it's best if the pilot uses a quantized model variant we already have in the catalog. Pinning a bleeding-edge variant will increase memory and cache churn and raise the chance of eviction.
- Telemetry: ops will need a read-only view into the token-level latency traces for the sprint; we should scope Data & Privacy.
- Roadmap alignment: we have a performance rollout scheduled for Dec that may affect the runtime kernel selection. If we commit a non-preemptible 24/7 carve, it could block a canary. Suggest limiting hard pins to the daytime window unless the customer signs a short term commitment.

I’ve attached a draft SLA exception note (sla-exception-request.pdf) that outlines risk, rollback, and monitoring requirements. Product can own the post-mortem and model variant recommendation.

If Sales can confirm customer willingness to sign a 6-month reservation, Product is comfortable escalating to a fuller carve. Otherwise accept the daytime-only carve Jonas proposed.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term carve for ClearHealth AI onboarding sprint

Looping back after customer sync this afternoon. ClearHealth is prepared to: 

- Accept a daytime-only non-preemptible carve for Nov 20–29 (08:00–20:00 UTC) if we provide the monitoring hooks and a short rollback playbook.
- Sign a 6-month reserved contract contingent on a successful onboarding (they want commercial terms finalized by Nov 30).

I’ve updated the HubSpot deal with the notes and attached the customer's confirmation screenshot inline (they sent an email). HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4981.

Kimberly — please confirm you want Ops to proceed with the 2x -> 4x scaling plan Jonas outlined (start at 2x pinned daytime and scale to 4x if capacity allows). If yes, Jonas — please open the carve ticket and add the monitoring dashboard and runbook checklist to INFRA-7382.

Thanks everyone — this is a good pilot to prove our low-latency offering for regulated health customers.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
